rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, late, or across the full range so later runs can trim phi0/phi1 and adjust slope or temperature.

All compounds eluted well within the broad scout, so trim the gradient window to the actual elution region to improve efficiency and likely raise CRF without sacrificing coverage. This narrower window should keep all peaks inside the gradient while testing whether the critical mid-cluster gains resolution under a less wasteful slope.

The trimmed window was far too weak, so revert to the broad solvent range and now probe slope response by halving tG. Comparing this with injection 1 will show whether the tight 6–7 region is slope-sensitive while also likely improving the time term if resolution remains acceptable.

The 6–7 region clearly worsened at the steeper 10 min gradient, so move to an intermediate slope between 10 and 20 min to recover that critical resolution while preserving a strong time advantage. This should map the CRF optimum versus tG near the current best method.

The optimum appears near tG 14–20 min, with the critical 6–7 pair improving as the gradient is made shallower. Test 16 min to see if that pair crosses fully acceptable resolution while keeping the run short enough to preserve the excellent time term.

The critical pair is slope-sensitive but already acceptable at 16 min, so temperature is now the best lever to seek a selectivity gain without giving up much speed. A modest decrease to 35 C may alter the close mid-cluster ordering/separation and potentially improve on the 14 min, zero-time-penalty method.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity in the central cluster, so test the opposite direction at 45 C to see whether the critical close pair separates better. This keeps the currently optimal slope while probing temperature as the remaining plausible route to exceed the best CRF.

Temperature shifts worsened selectivity, so return to 40 C and refine slope around the evident optimum by testing 18 min. This will show whether a slightly shallower gradient than 16 min can maintain full resolution while keeping the time penalty small enough to beat the current best.

With slope and temperature mapped, the next lever is the starting strength: raising phi0 slightly may shift the early/mid cluster selectivity enough to open the critical pair while preserving a short run. Keep phi1 and tG at the best settings so any change can be attributed mainly to the altered low-end gradient window.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved CRF, so continue in that direction to test whether a slightly stronger start further enhances selectivity in the critical 6–7 region while keeping the run comfortably short. This is a focused local optimization around the current best method.

The best method already has a short run, so trim the high-end window slightly by lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 while keeping the successful phi0 and tG. This may improve selectivity in the central cluster without risking late elution, since the last peak is still very early.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical pair and gave the best CRF so far, so continue trimming the upper gradient limit slightly. With the last peak still early, phi1 0.85 is a safe next step to test whether selectivity can be nudged the final increment toward the maximum.

We have already reached the maximum CRF, so this run is a confirmation-style local robustness check around the optimum by slightly increasing phi0 while keeping the successful upper limit and slope. It tests whether the score plateau extends nearby without repeating the exact best method.

Since the maximum score persists at phi0 0.15, step phi0 up once more to map the extent of the optimum plateau while keeping the successful phi1/tG/T fixed. This explores whether the method can be made even more front-loaded without sacrificing complete elution or critical-pair resolution.

The optimum region seems centered near phi1 0.85, so test one further reduction in phi1 while keeping the proven phi0 0.10 and tG 14. This checks the lower edge of the high-end window that still keeps all peaks eluting with full resolution.

Both phi0 0.10/phi1 0.85 and phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85 gave the maximum score, so test the adjacent corner phi0 0.15/phi1 0.90 to define the full high-scoring plateau. This maps robustness near the optimum without repeating a known best method.

Map the remaining corner of the apparent optimum region by lowering phi0 to 0.05 while keeping the successful phi1 0.85 and tG 14. This completes the local window study and tests whether the maximum-score plateau also extends to the lowest starting strength.

Now that the optimum composition window is identified, test whether a slightly steeper gradient can preserve full resolution while shaving time within the same phi window. This probes whether the score-1.000 solution is uniquely tied to tG 14 or extends to a faster method.

The faster 12 min run lost too much critical-pair resolution, so test the opposite side of the optimum window at 16 min within the best composition range. This checks whether full resolution is retained with only a minimal time sacrifice, and whether the score-1.000 plateau extends in tG as well.

With the tG optimum confirmed at 14 min, use the remaining runs to map the exact borders of the score-1.000 region in composition space. This combination probes whether the maximum plateau extends diagonally toward slightly higher phi0 and lower phi1.

Test the opposite diagonal corner near the optimum to complete the local composition map around the score-1.000 methods. This will define whether the plateau is bounded more by low phi0 or by high phi1.

With the composition plateau mapped and score 1.000 already achieved, use a remaining run to test robustness of the best composition at a higher temperature. This checks whether the maximum is narrowly tied to 40 C or whether the optimized phi window buffers moderate thermal selectivity changes.

A higher temperature destabilized the critical pair at the best composition, so use a remaining run to test the other thermal direction on the alternate score-1.000 method. This gives a final robustness check around the optimum while avoiding repetition of prior conditions.

One high-temperature point at 45 C showed a strong selectivity collapse for the critical pair; testing 50 C will reveal whether that effect is monotonic or whether a reordered selectivity regime emerges at still higher temperature. With only two runs left and the maximum already reached, this is a useful final mechanistic probe around the best composition.

For the final run, probe the last untested temperature corner adjacent to the score-1.000 plateau: phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85 at 45 C. This complements the 35 C result on the same composition and completes the thermal mapping around one of the optimum methods.
